To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of a 3D-printed, patient-specific, custom-made, cranial radiotherapy mask, in combination with a 3D conformal radiation therapy plan, is a feasible, safe, and efficacious method for delivering cranial radiotherapy for the treatment of brain metastasis in patients with breast cancer.
The use of whole brain radio therapy for brain metastases is associated with a decline in neurocognitive function.

1) the majority of patients with brain cancer have impaired neurocognition at diagnosis, 2) the neurocognitive effects of whole-brain radiation therapy and chemotherapy are additive, and 3) hippocampal-sparing radiotherapy may improve verbal memory and reduce neurotoxicity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of radiation on the brain and the development of strategies to prevent and/or reverse radiation-induced brain injury.
the development of novel therapeutic approaches for brain metastases.
the neurocognitive effects of whole brain radiotherapies, and with the potential of new technologies, such as hippocampal avoidance and radiosurgery, to reduce neurotoxicity.

we are not able to show that the use of a specific type of radiation therapy for brain metastasis, either whole brain or stereotactic radiosurgical, is superior to the other.

the neurocognitive effects of whole brain radio- therapy are not as severe as previously believed.
